name: Kentucky
tagline: Horse farms behind stone fences, coal-town hollows and two rivers' worth of ferry landings.
intro: Kentucky's byways wind between the plank and limestone fences of the Bluegrass horse farms, climb into the coal country of the Cumberland Plateau, follow Daniel Boone's road north from Cumberland Gap, and run along the Ohio and the Mississippi. This chapter follows the Scenic Byways and Highways program of the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, whose 2016 list names each route; KYTC does not say which are byways and which are highways, so lines drawn from its route layer are labelled scenic highways.

members.name: Abraham Lincoln Heritage Highway
members.blurb: US 150 east from Bardstown over the knobs to Springfield, a short drive from the farmhouse of Lincoln's uncle Mordecai, then on to the cannon-marked fields at Perryville, fought over in October 1862, and Danville.
members.note: The national Lincoln Heritage Scenic Highway joins this road with the Old Kentucky Turnpike below, and the line shown is the national one.

members.name: Big Bone Lick/Middle Creek Parkway
members.blurb: Boone County back roads to the sulfur springs at Big Bone Lick, where a salt lick drew mammoths and mastodons, and where Meriwether Lewis and later William Clark came to dig up their bones.

members.name: Blues to Bluegrass Scenic Byway (Bill Monroe Bluegrass Trail)
members.blurb: Ohio County roads to Rosine, where Bill Monroe lies in the town cemetery and pickers fill the general store on Friday nights, then north through Hawesville to the Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame in Owensboro.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Blues to Bluegrass Scenic Byway (Everly Brothers Rock-N-Roll Trail)
members.blurb: KY 56 and KY 81 through Sebree and Calhoun into Muhlenberg County and on through Central City, which has swallowed up Brownie, the settlement where Don Everly was born in 1937.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Blues to Bluegrass Scenic Byway (W.C. Handy Blues Trail)
members.blurb: US 60 west from Owensboro to Henderson on its red clay bluffs over the Ohio, where W. C. Handy met his wife at a barbecue in 1896 and a blues and barbecue festival still comes each June.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Boone Creek Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A short loop east of Lexington down into the valley of Boone's Creek, where Grimes Mill Road passes an 1803 stone mill with walls three and a half feet thick, the clubhouse of a fox hunt since 1928.
members.note: Route line from KYTC; the 2022 national dataset drew this road in the wrong place.

members.name: Cordell Hull Highway
members.blurb: From the gate of Mammoth Cave through Glasgow and south over hill and hollow toward Tennessee, near the twelve-cornered log meetinghouse of 1804 where Daniel Boone's sister Hannah is buried.

members.name: Country Music Highway
members.blurb: US 23 from the Virginia line to the Ohio River by Pikeville and Paintsville, with a sign at every county line naming the singers who came from there. Loretta Lynn's Butcher Holler lies in the hills near Van Lear.

members.name: Cumberland Cultural Heritage Highway
members.blurb: KY 90 around Lake Cumberland from Burkesville to Monticello and on to the lodge at Cumberland Falls, where the river drops 68 feet and a moonbow often hangs in the spray on full-moon nights.

members.name: Daniel Boone Heritage Trail
members.note: KY 418 in Clark County, on KYTC's route layer since 2020 but not on the 2016 list. Route line from KYTC.

members.name: Duncan Hines Scenic Tour
members.blurb: A loop from the old Bowling Green home of Duncan Hines, the restaurant-guide writer born in that town, north through Brownsville and across the Green River on the Mammoth Cave ferry.

members.name: Great River Road
members.blurb: The Mississippi bank of Kentucky from the Tennessee line to Wickliffe, past a bluff at Columbus where a Civil War chain with eleven-inch links once spanned the river, and the Mississippian mounds near the mouth of the Ohio.

members.name: Highway 524 Loop
members.blurb: A loop off US 42 out to Westport, a river hamlet of about 250 people on the Ohio whose post office opened in 1815, and back again to the highway.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Hughes Lane
members.blurb: Two miles of country lane north of Lexington from Russell Cave Road over to Paris Pike, whose dry-laid limestone fences were taken apart and relaid by hand when the highway was rebuilt.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Ironworks Pike
members.blurb: KY 1973 west from Paris Pike between horse farms to the Kentucky Horse Park, where Man o' War lies beneath his own statue near the gate.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: KY 160-Black Mountain
members.blurb: Up Looney Creek through Benham and Lynch, coal towns built by International Harvester and U.S. Steel, then up Black Mountain, at 4,145 feet the roof of Kentucky, to the Virginia line.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: KY 89
members.blurb: Thirty-five miles of KY 89 from the Rockcastle County line into McKee, the only town in Jackson County, which sits inside the Daniel Boone National Forest, and on north toward Irvine.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Mary Ingles Highway
members.blurb: KY 8 through the river town of Augusta, where a ferry still crosses the Ohio, on a highway named for Mary Ingles, who escaped her Shawnee captors in 1755 and walked home to Virginia.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: North Cleveland Road
members.blurb: KY 1973 north from Athens, a crossroads village chartered in 1826 that keeps its Greek Revival and Italianate storefronts, through rural eastern Fayette County to Winchester Road.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Old Frankfort Pike
members.blurb: KY 1681 out of Lexington under a canopy of hardwoods, between miles of dry-laid limestone fences and thoroughbred pastures, past the old Woodburn Stud where Kentucky's racehorse breeding began.
members.note: Now a National Scenic Byway as well (the Old Frankfort Pike Historic and Scenic Byway); KYTC's 2016 list predates that.

members.name: Old Kentucky Turnpike
members.blurb: US 31E through the Kentucky knobs from the log cabin of Lincoln's birth, kept inside a 1911 memorial hall, by way of Hodgenville to Bardstown and Federal Hill, the house remembered in Stephen Foster's 'My Old Kentucky Home'.

members.name: Old Richmond Road and Grimes Mill Road
members.blurb: Out of Lexington past Jacobson Park and over the interstate onto Grimes Mill Road as far as McCalls Mill Road, a little short of the Grimes family's old stone mill on Boone's Creek.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Pine Mountain Road
members.blurb: US 119 out of Whitesburg and up over Pine Mountain, a ridge 125 miles long that only two streams have managed to cut through, crossing the Little Shepherd Trail on the way down to Oven Fork.

members.name: Pisgah Pike
members.blurb: Five miles of Woodford County farm road from US 60 up to Old Frankfort Pike, through Pisgah, settled by Virginians in 1784, where the Presbyterian church has stood since 1812.
members.note: Route line from KYTC; the 2022 national dataset drew this road in the wrong place.

members.name: Red River Gorge Scenic Byways
members.blurb: A loop through the Daniel Boone National Forest that enters the gorge by Nada Tunnel, a one-lane bore cut through sandstone for a 1911 logging railroad, then winds below cliffs among more than a hundred natural arches.

members.name: Ridgetop Scenic Byway
members.blurb: KY 89 through Estill County, down to the Kentucky River at Irvine and out again, in a county where iron was smelted from 1810 and the ruins of the old furnaces still stand.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: River Road
members.blurb: Seven miles of River Road from Prospect into Louisville, ending at Zorn Avenue beside the 1860 water tower, a 183-foot Doric column on a Corinthian portico above the Ohio.

members.name: Riverboat Row
members.blurb: One mile of the Newport riverbank, facing Cincinnati across the Ohio, past moored riverboats and floating restaurants and the bridge locals call the Purple People Bridge, to James Taylor City Park.

members.name: Russell Cave Road
members.blurb: Two and a half miles of KY 353 in the horse country north of Lexington, from Iron Works Pike up to Hughes Lane, one link in a web of designated farm roads around Paris Pike.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Shakertown Road
members.blurb: A short run of US 68 between hand-laid stone fences into Pleasant Hill, where the Shakers lived from 1805 to 1910 in big stone and brick dwellings set along stone walks.
members.note: Route line from KYTC: the 2.4 miles of US 68 either side of the Pleasant Hill entrance. The 2022 national dataset drew a much longer stretch.

members.name: US 42
members.blurb: Fourteen miles of US 42 through Oldham County from Goshen, past the horses at Hermitage Farm, with a short loop that bends toward the Ohio River.

members.name: US 62-Midway-Versailles Road
members.blurb: Six miles of US 62 from Midway, laid out in 1835 as Kentucky's first railroad town, to Versailles, past thoroughbred farms with names like Fawn Leap and Shadowlawn.

members.name: US 68
members.blurb: The old buffalo road across the Bluegrass between plank and limestone fences, from Maysville by Lexington and Harrodsburg to Lebanon, then west through Bowling Green and Hopkinsville toward Paducah, past the 351-foot obelisk at Fairview.
members.note: KYTC lists two designations, US 68 east of Lebanon and US Highway 68 west of it; both are drawn as one road here.

members.name: Van Meter, Rice, and Elkchester Roads
members.blurb: Six miles of back roads west of Lexington, Van Meter Road and then Rice and Elkchester, that tie Versailles Road, where Keeneland stands, to the stone fences of Old Frankfort Pike.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Wilderness Road Heritage Highway
members.blurb: US 25E and US 25 north from the Cumberland Gap country along much of Daniel Boone's 1775 trail, by way of the Renfro Valley barn dance stage to the craft shops of Berea.

members.name: Winchester Road Corridor
members.blurb: Almost five miles of US 60 east from the edge of Lexington's urban service area, the first urban growth boundary in the country when it was drawn in 1958, out to the Clark County line.
members.note: Route line from KYTC (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Woodlands Trace
members.blurb: A ridge road down the middle of Land Between the Lakes, with Kentucky Lake to one side and Lake Barkley to the other, and a paved loop through a 700-acre prairie where elk and bison roam.

members.name: Zollicoffer-Thomas Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Ten miles from the national cemetery at Nancy across the fields where Felix Zollicoffer fell in January 1862, then down Old Mill Springs Battlefield Road to the ferry landing, the last stop on the battlefield tour.
members.note: KYTC's full name is The Zollicoffer-Thomas Scenic Byway (KY 235 Mill Springs Battlefield). Route line from KYTC; the national dataset folds it into the Cumberland Cultural Heritage Highway.

sources.label: KYTC, Kentucky State and National Scenic Byways and Highways (2016)
